title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Lines 1–3 finish a general argument begun on the previous page. Let 𝒢 be an extension of a profinite group Γ by an abelian group M, and E an M-torsor. Lifts of the Γ-action to E correspond to isomorphisms between the extension Aff(E) and 𝒢. Such lifts exist iff the class c²(𝒢) in H²(Γ,M) vanishes. When they exist, they form a torsor under Z¹(Γ,M). Taking E = M (the trivial torsor), M-conjugacy classes of lifts correspond to M-conjugacy classes of splittings of 𝒢, a torsor under H¹(Γ,M).

The main part of the page applies this to a specific case.
- Space: X = U_{0,3,Q̄}, the projective line minus {0,1,∞} over Q̄.
- Group: Γ = Π_Q × 𝔖_3 = N_{0,3}, i.e. Gal(Q̄/Q) times the symmetric group S_3 permuting the three punctures.
- Γ-equivariant coverings of X are the same as 𝔖_3-equivariant coverings of U_{0,3,Q}, i.e. coverings of the quotient stack (U_{0,3,Q}, 𝔖_3).

Using the constructions of §49 VI, Grothendieck forms a geometric metabelian-type quotient. A crossed-out version reads SL(2,Z)^/[Π̂_{0,3},Π̂_{0,3}]. The retained version is 𝔊^{+∧}/μ_𝔊 ≅ 𝔊^+_{0,3}/[Π̂_{0,3},Π̂_{0,3}] = M̃.
- Underlying fact: Γ(2)/±1 ≅ F_2 = π_1(U_{0,3}), and PSL_2(Z)/(Γ(2)/±1) ≅ S_3.
- So M̃ is the extension of 𝔖_3 by M^ = Π̂_{0,3}^{ab} ≅ Ẑ(1)², with S_3 acting through its standard 2-dimensional representation.

The group G_{ρ,σ̃} 'of the preceding sections' is the semidirect product Ẑ^*·M̃. It is an extension of Ẑ^* × 𝔖_3 by M^, where Ẑ^* acts on M^ through the cyclotomic structure.

There is a canonical homomorphism from the arithmetic version, the arithmetic fundamental group of the stack modulo [Π̂,Π̂], to G_{ρ,σ̃}. It fits into a map of exact sequences (drawn on the next page) whose right-hand map is χ × id, with χ the cyclotomic character. In other words, the arithmetic metabelian extension is the pullback of G along χ × id.

Purpose (completed on the next page):
- G splits, with a unique M^-conjugacy class of splittings.
- So the arithmetic extension splits with a canonical, though not unique, conjugacy class of splittings. Non-uniqueness comes from H¹(Γ_Q, Ẑ(1)²), which is Kummer-type.
- Splitting also follows from the existence of the Fermat tower, which is defined over Q with S_3-symmetry.
- The result is a canonical class of descents of the abelianized tower of X to the stack (M_{0,3,Q}, 𝔖_3), viewed as a functor on its fundamental groupoid.
errors: Notational clash: M̃ is first defined as a geometric quotient 𝔊^{+∧}/μ, an extension of 𝔖_3 by M^. A few lines later M̃ = M_{0,3}/(Π̂_{0,3},Π̂_{0,3}) denotes the arithmetic extension of Γ = Π_Q×𝔖_3 by M^, which maps to G_{ρ,σ̃}. The left marginal note seems to flag this ('M devient M_{0,3}, Π devient Π_{0,3}', '... en notant M̃!').

The claim (next page) that G splits with a unique M^-conjugacy class requires H¹(Ẑ^*×𝔖_3, M^) = 0. For l odd this is clear: the torsion of Z_l^* acts through a nontrivial character. For l = 2, H¹({±1}, Z_2(1)) = Z/2, so vanishing would have to come from the 𝔖_3-part. This is not checked on this page, so it is a minor gap.

ideas.what: Lifts of a Γ-action to an M-torsor correspond to isomorphisms of extensions; the obstruction lies in H², and conjugacy classes of splittings are a torsor under H¹.
ideas.modern_name: Classification of group extensions / nonabelian descent via group cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane; Giraud for the torsor and gerbe language
ideas.where_published: Standard; used throughout SGA 1 exposé XIII and in La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Γ_Q×S_3-equivariant coverings of P^1−{0,1,∞} over Q̄ are identified with coverings of the stack (U_{0,3,Q}, S_3), with PSL_2(Z)^ ⊃ Π̂_{0,3} and quotient S_3.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic fundamental group of the stack [M_{0,4}/S_3]; Galois action on the profinite (modular) tower
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984); La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Metabelian quotient π_1/[Π̂,Π̂]: an extension of Γ by Π̂^{ab} = Ẑ(1)², pulled back from a split extension of Ẑ^*×S_3 via the cyclotomic character; splitting via the Fermat tower.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the abelianized fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}; Fermat curves; Ihara's universal power series / Anderson–Ihara
ideas.where_published: unsure (possibly sketched in Longue Marche continuation only)

missed.claim: In reading the 1980s papers (apparently Ihara-type work on G_{ρ,σ}), Grothendieck explicitly frames the splitting of the metabelian extension as a consequence of his general torsor/extension formalism plus the Fermat tower. He packages the outcome as a canonical (non-unique) M^-conjugacy class of descent data, i.e. a functor on the fundamental groupoid of the stack (M_{0,3,Q}, 𝔖_3). This is a reformulation of known results, not a new theorem.
missed.quote: un foncteur sur Π(M_{0,3 Q}, 𝔖_3), de groupes ou groupes profinis
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical documentation of Grothendieck's engagement with the Ihara / Anderson–Ihara metabelian theory and his stacky viewpoint on it. The mathematics itself is in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page combines standard extension/torsor cohomology with a reformulation of known metabelian results (Fermat tower, cyclotomic pullback) for P^1−{0,1,∞}. It is historically interesting as evidence that Grothendieck was reading the Ihara-school results, but there is no new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'ladite extension 𝒢 de Γ par M' (script G as on the previous page), not 𝔖.
The quotient line reads '𝔊^{+∧}/μ_𝔊 ≃ 𝔊^+_{03}/[Π̂_{0,3},Π̂_{0,3}] = M̃' with script G, not 𝔖. The crossed-out version is '... ≃ SL(2,Z)^/[Π̂_{0,3},Π̂_{0,3}]'.
'les Γ-revêtements de X correspondant aux 𝔖_3-revêtements de U_{0,3 Q}, i.e. aux rev. de (U_{0,3 Q}, 𝔖_3)': the '[?]' is 'de'.
The semidirect product reads 'G_{ρ,σ̃} = Ẑ^*·M̃', 'ext. de Ẑ^*×𝔖_3 par M^'.
Left margin reads approximately: 'NB La question qui se pose ici: M devient M_{0,3}, Π devient Π_{0,3}'. Second margin: '... en notant M̃!'
